## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
library(mdsr)
library(sf)
library(ggspatial)
library(leaflet)
library(tidyverse)
```


When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
#Reading Data
full_data <- read_csv("../data/combined_data.csv")

# Create sf object for US counties
states_map <- maps::map("state", region = ".",
                       plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)|>  st_as_sf()

#Hard coded vector for states
state_abre <- c( "alabama" = "AL", "arizona" = "AZ", "arkansas" = "AR",
  "california" = "CA", "colorado" = "CO", "connecticut" = "CT",
  "delaware" = "DE", "district of columbia" = "DC", "florida" = "FL",
  "georgia" = "GA", "idaho" = "ID", "illinois" = "IL", "indiana" = "IN",
  "iowa" = "IA", "kansas" = "KS", "kentucky" = "KY", "louisiana" = "LA",
  "maine" = "ME", "maryland" = "MD", "massachusetts" = "MA", "michigan" = "MI",
  "minnesota" = "MN", "mississippi" = "MS", "missouri" = "MO", "montana" = "MT",
  "nebraska" = "NE", "nevada" = "NV", "new hampshire" = "NH",
  "new jersey" = "NJ", "new mexico" = "NM", "new york" = "NY", 
  "north carolina" = "NC", "north dakota" = "ND", "ohio" = "OH",
  "oklahoma" = "OK", "oregon" = "OR", "pennsylvania" = "PA",
  "rhode island" = "RI", "south carolina" = "SC", "south dakota" = "SD",
  "tennessee" = "TN", "texas" = "TX", "utah" = "UT", "vermont" = "VT",
  "virginia" = "VA", "washington" = "WA", "west virginia" = "WV",
  "wisconsin" = "WI", "wyoming" = "WY")

#Recode and leftjoin to create dataset with the location
states_map <- states_map |>
  mutate(State = recode(ID, !!!state_abre)) |> select(-ID)
full_data_with_state <- left_join(states_map, full_data , by = "State")

#All unique months (chronologically) and filter which one we want
unique_months <- sort(unique(full_data_with_state$month))
month_variable = unique_months[2]
month_name <- format(as.Date(month_variable), "%B %Y")
full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |> 
  filter(month == month_variable)

#Create a plot for the specific month
Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month, 
                  aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular)) +
  geom_sf() +
  scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Average Regular Gas Price by State,"),
    subtitle = "Real (inflation-adjusted) prices per gallon",
    fill = "Price ($/gal)",
    caption = paste("Month:", month_name))

Gasplot

plotly::ggplotly(Gasplot)

```



You can add options to executable code like this 


```{r}
# Creating scale for every month so shades are comparable across months
price_limits <- range(full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular, na.rm = TRUE)

# Empty list to then fill with the plots
month_plots <- list()
# For loop to create a different month in each index
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  #Filtering for the unique month
  month_variable <- unique_months[i]
  month_name <- format(as.Date(month_variable), "%B %Y")
  full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |> 
    filter(month == month_variable)
  #Creating plot
  Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month, 
                    aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular)) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1, limits = price_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Average Regular Gas Price by State,", month_name),
      subtitle = "Real (inflation-adjusted) prices per gallon",
      fill = "Price ($/gal)",
      caption = paste("Month:", month_name))
  #Add it to month_plots
  month_plots[[i]] <- Gasplot}

# Replicating the list but for plotly instead of ggplot
plotly_plots <- list()
for (i in seq_along(month_plots)) {
  plotly_plots[[i]] <- plotly_build(ggplotly(month_plots[[i]]))}

# This step is probably the most confusing, so I had to learn a bit about how
# Plotly works. Each month's plot in plotly_plots has its own set of
# "traces", that together produces the plot and we need to group these traces 
# so that Plotly knows what to display for each month.

# Empty list that will collect the trace from every month
all_traces <- list()
# Empty vector to record which month each trace came from.
trace_month <- c()
# Go through each month's plotly plot, one at a time
for (i in seq_along(plotly_plots)) {
  # Grab this month's traces (the pieces that draw its map)
  month_traces <- plotly_plots[[i]]$x$data
  
  # Add them to the end of the big list
  all_traces <- c(all_traces, month_traces)
  
  # Add one label per trace saying "this came from month i".
  # rep(i, n) repeats i n times, e.g. rep(2, 3) gives 2 2 2
  trace_month <- c(trace_month, rep(i, length(month_traces)))
}

# Hide every trace except month 1's.
# trace_month[j] == 1 is TRUE for month 1 traces and FALSE for all others,
# and that TRUE/FALSE becomes the trace's "visible" setting.
# Without this, all months would be drawn on top of each other.
for (j in seq_along(all_traces)) {
  all_traces[[j]]$visible <- trace_month[j] == 1
}

# Copy month 1's figure to keep its layout, title and settings,
# then replace its traces with the full list from every month
combined <- plotly_plots[[1]]
combined$x$data <- all_traces

# Check: should look exactly like month 1 (the other months are there, just hidden)
combined

# Check: total number of traces, and how many each month contributed.
# Top row = month number, bottom row = number of traces for that month.
# Counts differ because not every state has data every month.
length(all_traces)
table(trace_month)

```



```{r}
# Creating scale for every month so shades are comparable across months
price_limits <- range(full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular, na.rm = TRUE)
price_limits









# Your original plot, wrapped in a function of the month
make_month_plot <- function(m) {
  full_data_with_state |>
    filter(month == m) |>
    ggplot(aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular)) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1, limits = price_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(
      title = "Gas",
      subtitle = "Gas",
      fill = "Real Prices",
      caption = paste("Month:", as.character(m)))
}

# One ggplot per month, each converted to plotly
# (purrr:: prefix needed because maps::map masks purrr::map)
month_plots <- purrr::map(unique_months, make_month_plot)
built_plots <- purrr::map(month_plots, ~ plotly_build(ggplotly(.x)))

# Stack every month's traces into one figure, remembering which month each belongs to
all_traces  <- list()
trace_month <- c()
for (i in seq_along(built_plots)) {
  tr <- built_plots[[i]]$x$data
  all_traces  <- c(all_traces, tr)
  trace_month <- c(trace_month, rep(i, length(tr)))
}

# Show only the first month to start
for (j in seq_along(all_traces)) {
  all_traces[[j]]$visible <- trace_month[j] == 1
}

combined <- built_plots[[1]]
combined$x$data <- all_traces

# Slider: each step turns on one month's traces and updates the title
steps <- purrr::map(seq_along(unique_months), function(i) {
  list(
    method = "update",
    label  = as.character(unique_months[i]),
    args   = list(
      list(visible = trace_month == i),
      list(title = list(text = paste("Gas —", as.character(unique_months[i]))))
    )
  )
})

combined$x$layout$title   <- list(text = paste("Gas —", as.character(unique_months[1])))
combined$x$layout$sliders <- list(list(
  active = 0,
  currentvalue = list(prefix = "Month: "),
  pad = list(t = 30),
  steps = steps
))

combined
```


The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
